topics: Burst rehearsal plan and traffic generator
Fallback model routing and QoS degradation strategy
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2027-07-22 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Reilly (Redwood SE), Priya Narang (Redwood CSM); Rajiv Patel (Neptune Head of Platform), Ana Gomez (SRE Lead), Tom Kessler (CTO), Sasha Ivanov (Infra)

Summary (auto): tune autoscale, rehearse burst, fallback policies, next steps.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for jumping on. Agenda for today is autoscale policy fine-tune, runbook for burst rehearsals, and contingency routing. Quick check — everyone good with that?
[00:12] Rajiv Patel: Yep that works. We're mostly looking to validate burst behavior and make sure we don't blow budget during spikes so prioritizing graceful degradation.
[00:25] Liam O'Reilly: Great. I'll surface the policy changes we tried last sprint and the telemetry we pulled. Note, some of the numbers are a little noisy because of how the sampler hooks are set.
[00:38] Ana Gomez: FYI our traces show multiple short spikes in the 10-12 second range, not long sustained increases. That matters for cooldown windows.
[00:50] Maya Chen: Good, so we probably want a shorter scale-up window but a slightly longer cooldown to avoid flip‑flopping. Thoughts?
[00:58] Tom Kessler: My gut says shorter scale-up and immediate eviction of low-priority jobs. But we need fallback routing too, so user-facing requests keep going albeit at lower quality.
[01:12] Liam O'Reilly: Right, the platform supports model variant routing. We can route to a lower-cost quantized variant for non-critical routes. However, we also watch KV cache hit rate — if cache warms back up quickly, routing back is cheap.
[01:30] Sasha Ivanov: Two quick Qs: 1) does the Dedicated partition allow preemptible burst nodes? 2) what happens to in-flight streams if we trigger fallback mid-response?
[01:44] Maya Chen: Good questions. For (1) yes, we can configure burst pools with lower-priority nodes; for (2) the runtime will gracefully finish in-flight tokens on current model then switch new requests to fallback — there's a short tail effect. We have example logs in the shared drive.
[02:05] Rajiv Patel: Can you add the expected latency delta when falling back? Engineers here need a ballpark.
[02:12] Liam O'Reilly: From our tests, fallback to the q4_8bit variant added roughly 70-120ms p95 on generation in synthetic loads, but token throughput sometimes improved because of smaller kernel overhead. Caveat: your prompt lengths matter.
[02:30] Ana Gomez: That's acceptable if we can cap the rate. Our SLA tolerance is p95 < 800ms.
[02:38] Maya Chen: Ok noted. Next up: autoscale params. Liam, show the policy you propose.
[02:45] Liam O'Reilly: I'm proposing: scale-up on 60% GPU util sustained for 18s, step of +2 replicas, max burst to +6 for 10 minutes; scale-down after 180s of low-util with step -1, min replicas 2. Also a cooldown of 45s after scale-up before next scale.
[03:07] Rajiv Patel: 18s sustain seems short given our spike profile, which is spikes of 8–12s, they'll not trigger scale-up. We want to capture those bursts.
[03:19] Liam O'Reilly: Good catch, we made that conservative to avoid noisy scaling. If you want to capture 10s spikes, we can lower sustain to 8–10s but keep a stricter max burst cap. Another approach: allow rapid ephemeral burst that doesn't instantiate heavy replicas but uses reserved burst nodes.
[03:35] Tom Kessler: Reserved burst nodes sound safer — cost predictable. What's the reserve granularity?
[03:41] Maya Chen: We can reserve in increments of GPU units; typical is 1–4 GPUs for a burst pool. You can pre-commit a small burst pool and let autoscale tap it.
[03:50] Ana Gomez: How does prefix/KV cache behave if we move traffic to burst nodes? Do we suffer cache miss storm?
[03:58] Liam O'Reilly: If burst nodes are cold, yes initially you'll see miss rate spike. We suggest warm-up prefetch for the most common prefixes during rehearsal, and also to enable shared KV snapshots if you use Dedicated with shared storage.
[04:14] Rajiv Patel: Warm-up prefetch—can you outline steps? We need an automated plan for nightly runs.
[04:20] Liam O'Reilly: Sure — script that replays top 500 prompts at low concurrency to populate cache, then a short wait. We'll include that in the runbook.
[04:30] Maya Chen: Priya, are we comfortable proposing the 48-hr Dedicated test partition next week?
[04:36] Priya Narang: Yes, SEs can provision it and we can monitor. We should agree what telemetry to collect — CPU/GPU util, cache hit/miss, request latency, queue length, and model switch events.
[04:48] Ana Gomez: Also the per-route token counts and any rate-limit tripping.
[04:53] Liam O'Reilly: We'll instrument per-route QoS metrics and push to the dashboard. We'll also attach a small synthetic client to generate controlled patterns.
[05:05] Tom Kessler: On fallback: if we route to lower-quality model, do we keep the same token billing? Cost implications matter.
[05:14] Maya Chen: Billing is per-token variant; cheaper model variants are lower cost per token. We'll provide cost delta estimates in the policy doc.
[05:22] Rajiv Patel: Useful. Also want to talk about circuit-breaker thresholds — e.g., stop accepting requests for non-critical endpoints if latency breaches a threshold.
[05:32] Liam O'Reilly: We can set per-route circuit breakers tied to error rate and latency. When triggered, routes can either be rejected with 429, queued, or downgraded to summary/shorter outputs.
[05:44] Ana Gomez: I prefer downgrade to shorter outputs over outright rejection for our user flows.
[05:50] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll recommend downgrade-first for user-facing, reject for backend batch jobs.
[05:58] Rajiv Patel: Can we see an example policy that combines reserved burst, ephemeral scale, and fallback routing?
[06:06] Liam O'Reilly: I'll upload a policy JSON with three sections: reservePools, autoscaleRules, fallbackRules. High level now: reserve pool 4 GPUs, autoscale trigger at 40% util for 10s with step +1, max ephemeral +4, fallback to q4_variant for routes tagged low_qos.
[06:26] Maya Chen: Great. Let's talk rehearsal plan. We want two rehearsals: a daytime peak and an end-of-day stress. We want to measure 1) cold-warm cache behavior 2) model switching latency 3) billing delta.
[06:40] Sasha Ivanov: For the daytime peak, can we simulate the same request mix as our real traffic? We'll share sample payloads.
[06:46] Liam O'Reilly: Yes, please send sample payloads. We'll parameterize concurrency and QPS.
[06:51] Rajiv Patel: How long does it take to provision the burst pool? If we need it for 10 minutes it's fine, but if it's 20–30 minutes then it doesn't help with short spikes.
[06:59] Maya Chen: Provisioning for reserved burst is instant within the Dedicated partition; for cold ephemeral nodes it can be on the order of 2–4 minutes depending on image pull and KV initialization. That's why reserved burst for short spikes is preferred.
[07:12] Ana Gomez: Are there safety knobs to prevent oscillation—like a hysteresis that prevents scale-down within X seconds after scale-up?
[07:21] Liam O'Reilly: Yes, that's the cooldown parameter; we also support multi-signal gating where both CPU and p95 latency must cross thresholds before scale-up. That reduces oscillation.
[07:33] Tom Kessler: Multi-signal sounds good. Can we gate scale-up on p95 > 650ms AND GPU util > 45%?
[07:40] Liam O'Reilly: Absolutely. We'll include a sample rule for that.
[07:46] Rajiv Patel: Ok, what about auditing and compliance — if we use burst nodes in another region for overflow, we have data residency issues.
[07:55] Maya Chen: Good point. We can set routing policies to ensure user data stays in region; overflow nodes must be region-matched or Private deployment used. We'll flag this in the runbook as a hard constraint.
[08:08] Ana Gomez: Also need SSO/SCIM mapping for who can initiate a rehearsal.
[08:13] Priya Narang: We'll add playbook steps requiring approval from platform owners before any live rehearsal.
[08:19] Maya Chen: Next: instrumentation details. Liam, quick list of dashboards we'll push.
[08:24] Liam O'Reilly: 1) Replicas over time, 2) GPU util + per-GPU memory, 3) Cache hit rate by prefix, 4) Request latency by route, 5) Model variant switch events. We'll also export raw logs to your S3 if you prefer.
[08:44] Sasha Ivanov: S3 export is ideal for our long-term analysis.
[08:48] Maya Chen: Great. Any blockers from your side for the 48-hr test?
[08:52] Rajiv Patel: Need legal sign-off for the temporary partition's data retention, and we'll need a simple NDA addendum for access.
[08:58] Tom Kessler: Also procurement might need a PO — what's the expected cost for 48-hr test with a small burst pool?
[09:05] Maya Chen: We'll provide an estimate in the policy doc — ballpark is $X per GPU hour, we'll give a range.
[09:12] Ana Gomez: One other small thing — does Redwood preserve request bodies in logs or only metadata? We need to ensure PII isn't stored.
[09:21] Priya Narang: By default we mask request bodies unless customers ask for full traces. We can enable field-level redaction.
[09:29] Rajiv Patel: Good. For rehearsals we'll request redaction still and provide synthetic payloads.
[09:35] Maya Chen: Perfect. Let's confirm deliverables and timeline.
[09:38] Liam O'Reilly: Deliverables: policy JSON, rehearsal runbook + scripts, provisioning the 48-hr Dedicated partition, instrumentation dashboard links, and cost delta estimates. I'll aim to have policy + runbook by 2027-07-24.
[09:52] Rajiv Patel: We'll send sample traces and payloads by 2027-07-27.
[09:57] Maya Chen: Priya will coordinate the provisioning window. Priya?
[10:01] Priya Narang: Yes, I'll schedule provisioning for 2027-07-28 and confirm with you all.
[10:07] Ana Gomez: Quick question — can we test fallback without actually swapping models by simulating response truncation?
[10:13] Liam O'Reilly: We have a 'soft degrade' mode that truncates responses or injects summarization without model swap; we'll include that as an option in the runbook.
[10:23] Tom Kessler: Good to have.
[10:27] Maya Chen: Alright let's do a short recap and close.
[10:30] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to share autoscale policy JSON and cost estimates by 2027-07-25; SE to provide runbook and rehearsal script by 2027-07-24; Neptune to share traces/payloads by 2027-07-27; schedule 48-hr Dedicated test for 2027-07-28. Agreed?
[10:47] Rajiv Patel: Agreed.
[10:50] Ana Gomez: Agreed.
[10:53] Tom Kessler: Agreed.
[10:55] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and attach the docs.
[11:00] (meeting ends)
